Yes, the value matches. The row with that titer is shown below (its titer is in mg/L, the same amount as the text's 5.83[1] g/L after unit conversion): 5830[2] in Table 2[3]. Its product is prodigiosin[4], its strain is JNB5–1 → SMCH[5], its strategy is Integration of proC, serC, and metH to enhance precursor supply[6], and its reference is [101][7]. This is the same work the text cites for the PG result: [101,117][8].

The strain names do not match. The text calls the engineered strain PG, but the row with the matching titer is named JNB5–1 → SMCH. The only entry in that table containing PG is JNB5–1 → PG-6[9], with titer 10,250[10] mg/L and reference [14][11]. That is a different value and reference, so it is not the 5.83[12] g/L result.
